message.content:
Sure! Below is a ready‑to‑run **curl** command (and a short Python snippet) that will post your comment to the IP `192.168.1.1` on VirusTotal.  
Just copy the command, paste it into a terminal, and hit **Enter**.  

> **⚠️ Security note** – keep your API key (`ABC321`) secret. Never share it in public forums or commit it to version control.

---

## 1️⃣ Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type": "comment",
           "attributes": {
             "text": "Confirmed #malware"
           }
         }'
```

### What this does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `-X POST` | Sends a POST request |
| URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` – the endpoint for adding a comment to that IP |
| `-H "x-apikey: ABC321"` | Your API key in the required header |
| `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` | Tells the server you’re sending JSON |
| `-d '{...}'` | The JSON payload you supplied |

If everything goes well, you’ll receive a JSON response that looks something like:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "some-comment-id",
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
      "text": "Confirmed #malware",
      "created_at": "2026-08-25T12:34:56Z",
      ...
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 2️⃣ Using Python (requests)

If you prefer Python, here’s a quick snippet:

```python
import requests
import json

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "ABC321",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=json.dumps(payload))

print("Status:", response.status_code)
print("Response:", response.json())
```

---

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `401 Unauthorized` | Wrong API key or missing header | Double‑check the key and that `x-apikey` is present |
| `400 Bad Request` | Malformed JSON or missing fields | Verify the JSON structure matches the example |
| `403 Forbidden` | Key doesn’t have permission to comment | Check your API key’s permissions in the VirusTotal dashboard |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded | Wait a minute or reduce request frequency |

---

That’s all you need! Once the request succeeds, your comment will appear in the VirusTotal UI under the IP’s “Comments” tab. If you run into any issues, let me know the exact error message and I’ll help troubleshoot further. Happy scanning!
